preconditions.expression: all(c in 'ab' for c in stdin.splitlines()[1])
preconditions.description: The second line of stdin is a string consisting only of characters 'a' and 'b'.

preconditions.expression: len(stdin.splitlines()[0].split()) == 2 and all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[0]) and all(c.isdigit() for c in stdin.splitlines()[0].split()[1])
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin contains exactly two integers n and k, where n is the length of the string and k is the maximum number of allowed character changes.
The integers n and k satisfy the constraints 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000 and 0 ≤ k ≤ n.

postconditions.expression: stdout.isdigit() and int(stdout) == max(max(len(list(group)) for group in itertools.groupby(s)) for s in possible_strings(n, k, stdin.splitlines()[1]))
postconditions.description: The output is an integer representing the maximum beauty achievable by changing at most k characters in the input string, where beauty is defined as the maximum length of a substring of equal characters ('a' or 'b'). The function possible_strings(n, k, s) generates all possible strings obtainable by changing at most k characters in s.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout) >= max(len(list(group)) for group in itertools.groupby(stdin.splitlines()[1]))
postconditions.description: The output is at least the beauty of the original string (i.e., the maximum length of a substring of equal characters in the original string).
